correctness.rationale: Centralizer=M2(Fq[t]/t^n) exactly. Every nonzero matrix splits uniquely by minimum t-valuation. In shallow strata, the primitive square-zero reduction is one Jordan conjugacy orbit with orbit-stabilizer size (q²−1)q^(2m−2); its lifts have uniformly distributed determinant in t^mR because a cofactor is a unit. Smith normal form gives each Fq-rank. Deep strata are all matrices over a shorter truncated polynomial ring, separated into invertible and rank-one residues; uniform determinant valuation again yields the exact rank polynomial. Exhaustive independent polynomial-arithmetic and linear-rank tests passed eight finite cases, and the rational formula passed 96 parameter consistency tests. The finite tests are not offered as proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The broader object family of all centralizer nilpotents does not imply individual square-zero rank counts. A stronger total over all matrices or a coarser entry-valuation partition is insufficient, since an entry-valuation stratum mixes several ranks. The proof computes the missing determinant valuation conditional on that stratum.

originality.rationale: The exact rank-by-rank polynomial is a strict refinement of a previously known total/entry-valuation census and of the 2022 Jordan-orbit existence theorem. Neither the total nor orbit existence implies the rank multiplicities; the determinant-valuation distribution is the additional result. Closest relevant primary texts were materially inspected; novelty remains conditional on unindexed equivalent formulations.
residual_risks: A rank distribution equivalent to this formula may be hidden in unindexed Hall-polynomial or finite-module representation counting literature.
The prior total/valuation census is a close antecedent; only rank-stratified coefficients and conditional determinant law are asserted as new.

value.rationale: For square-zero matrices the rank determines the full Jordan type. Counting every rank in the natural equal-double-block centralizer refines existing orbit-possibility classification to exact finite-field point counts for an infinite parameter family. The result is a complete geometric/arithmetic invariant with substantive determinant-valuation arguments, not merely a small numerical experiment.
